one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent wrote a sanitizer that never removed dangerous active-content tags (iframe, object, embed, frame), instead iteratively patching attribute-level vectors on self-authored tests that created false confidence without closing the structural coverage gaps required by the hidden test suite.
t_err_evidence: create the filter.py script ... uses BeautifulSoup ... remove JavaScript while preserving the rest of the HTML structure
t_commit_evidence: The incomplete implementation written at step 2 is the only substantive code produced; all subsequent edits (steps 7, 14, 21) only patch attribute-level handling (href whitespace, src attributes) and never add tag decomposition, so the outcome was structurally locked in at step 2.
trigger_explanation: The agent's plan to strip JavaScript was conceptually plausible but the generated implementation was structurally incomplete: it addressed attribute-level vectors (on* handlers, javascript: URLs) without recognizing that entire element categories (iframe, object, embed, frame) constitute independent XSS vectors that must be removed as tags, not just sanitized at the attribute level. This reflects a code-generation quality gap rather than a wrong assumption or ignored evidence.
